data.name: Hannibal
data.gender_notes: Hannibal is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Phoenician word hannibal, meaning 'graceful' or 'merciful'. The name became famous when the Carthaginian general Hannibal Barca led the Carthaginian army against the Roman Republic in the Second Punic War (218–201 BC). The name Hannibal carries the meaning “Graceful, merciful” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Hannibal usually hope their child will grow to embody graceful, merciful and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Encourages compassion and understanding towards others.
data.etymology: Hannibal belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Graceful, merciful.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Hannibal total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

in_hebrew.name: חננבל
in_hebrew.long_meaning: The Hebrew name Hannibal is derived from the Hebrew words 'חנן' (chanan) which means grace, and 'אל' (el) which means God. The name Hannibal thus means 'God is gracious' or 'grace from God'.

in_greek.name: Χαννίβαλ
in_greek.long_meaning: The Greek name Hannibal is derived from the Greek words 'χάννισκος' (channiskos) or 'χάννιβαλ' (channibal), which mean grace or mercy. The name Hannibal thus represents the idea of God's mercy or grace.

in_latin.name: Hannibal
in_latin.long_meaning: The Latin name Hannibal is derived from the Latin word 'hannibalus', which means grace or mercy. The name Hannibal thus represents the idea of God's mercy or grace.

in_english.name: Hannibal
